title: Allah swears by the pen and what it writes.
subtitle: Writing as a gift worth pausing over
then: The surah opens with the letter Nun, whose meaning is known to Allah. Then an oath by the pen. Ibn Kathir says this alerts people to a favor: {reward}Allah taught them writing, and through it knowledge is gained.{/reward} Some early scholars said it also points to {idea}the angels recording every deed.{/idea}
now: You type hundreds of words a day. Messages, notes, comments, a quick reply at midnight. Every one of them is a pen moving. {idea}Somewhere, your deeds are being written too.{/idea} The oath asks you to stop and notice both.
old: Writing is ordinary. Everyone can do it.
new: The ability to write and learn is a gift, and my own record is being written right now.
try: Before you send your next message today, reread it once as if it were going into your record.

title: The one they called mad was the sanest man there.
subtitle: A label from people who refused the truth
then: This is one of the earliest surahs, sent when opposition in Makkah had turned harsh. The chiefs called the Prophet ﷺ insane. Ibn Kathir explains they did this {trap}because they denied the clear truth he brought.{/trap} Allah answers directly: {reward}by your Lord's favor, you are not mad.{/reward}
now: You start praying at work, or stop joining the gossip, and someone says you have gone strange. The family group chat jokes that you have changed. {trap}A label is easier than an argument.{/trap} {idea}It often says more about the one who throws it.{/idea}
old: If people call me strange, maybe I am the problem.
new: When people cannot answer the truth, they label the person carrying it.
try: Think of one label someone gave you for doing right. Let it go with a quiet du'a for them.

title: A reward that never runs out.
subtitle: What patience under insults earns
then: Right after the insult comes the comfort. Ibn Kathir says the reward is for {idea}conveying the message and being patient with their abuse.{/idea} The word means it is {reward}never cut off{/reward}, and Mujahid said it is without reckoning.
now: You care for a sick parent and nobody notices. You keep your temper with a rude customer for the hundredth time. People forget by evening. {reward}Allah's reward for patience does not expire.{/reward}
old: If no one sees my patience, it was wasted.
new: Patience for Allah earns a reward that never stops, seen or unseen.
try: Do one patient thing today that no one will notice, and intend it only for Allah.

title: His character was the Quran, lived out.
subtitle: The answer to their insult was his conduct

row.title: never said uff
sub: ten years of service, Anas said

then: When A'ishah was asked about the character of the Prophet ﷺ, she said: {idea}his character was the Quran.{/idea} Anas served him for ten years and said he {reward}never once said a word of displeasure{/reward} or asked why something was or was not done.
now: Your kid spills juice on the laptop. Your coworker misses the deadline again. The urge is to snap, to say why did you do that. {idea}Ten years and not one uff.{/idea} That is the standard this verse praises.
old: Good character means being nice when it is easy.
new: Great character is living the Quran in the small moments that test you.
try: The next time someone makes a small mistake near you today, skip the why did you. Just help.

title: Wait. Both sides will see clearly soon.
subtitle: Truth does not need to win every argument now
then: The Prophet ﷺ was being mocked daily. Instead of telling him to argue back, Allah says: {idea}you will see, and they will see.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it means both he and his opponents {reward}will come to know{/reward} the truth.
now: Someone spreads a false story about you at work. You want to post a long reply tonight and prove everything. {trap}The urge to settle it all right now.{/trap} {idea}Some things are made clear by time and by Allah, not by you.{/idea}
old: If I do not defend myself now, the lie will win.
new: Truth comes out in its time. I can stay calm and keep doing right.
try: Pick one argument you are itching to win. Leave it unsent for 24 hours.

title: The real question: who was truly lost?
subtitle: The accusation turned back on the accusers
then: They said the Prophet ﷺ was the afflicted one. The verse turns the question around. Ibn Kathir says it means they will know {trap}who is insane and misguided{/trap} among them. Like the other verse: {idea}tomorrow they will know who is the liar.{/idea}
now: You are the only one at the table not drinking, or not laughing at the cruel joke. You feel like the odd one. {idea}Being the odd one is not the same as being wrong.{/idea} Ask the real question quietly in your heart.
old: If I am the only one, I must be the one who is off.
new: Being alone with the truth is not madness. Leaving the truth is.
try: Next time you feel like the odd one out for doing right, say silently: Allah knows who is guided.

title: Allah knows best who strayed and who is guided.
subtitle: The final judge of who is right
then: The argument in Makkah was loud. The chiefs had the crowd. This verse closes the matter: {idea}your Lord knows best{/idea} who has gone astray and who is guided. The verdict is {reward}not decided by the majority.{/reward}
now: Likes, views, the comment section, the opinion of your cousins. All of it votes on who you are. {trap}You can spend your life chasing that vote.{/trap} {idea}Only one opinion about your path really matters.{/idea}
old: What people think of me tells me if I am on the right path.
new: Only Allah truly knows who is guided, so His view is the one I live for.
try: Ask Allah once today: guide me, and keep me among those You know are guided.

title: Do not take orders from those who deny the truth.
subtitle: Staying firm when pressure is loud
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the verses before: {reward}just as We favored you with guidance and great character{/reward}, so do not obey the deniers. The surah introduction says the noise around the Prophet ﷺ was {trap}meant to scare him into giving in.{/trap}
now: Friends who laugh at your fasting. A manager who hints that honesty is naive. A feed that tells you faith is old fashioned. {trap}Pressure rarely says obey. It says relax.{/trap} {idea}You do not have to follow it.{/idea}
old: If enough people push, it is easier to just go along.
new: Their pressure does not get a vote over what Allah has given me.
try: Notice one voice today that pushes you away from your faith. Mute it, even for a day.

title: They wanted a deal: you soften, we soften.
subtitle: The quiet trap of compromise on truth
then: The chiefs offered a deal. Ibn Abbas said it meant {trap}you permit our idols, and we permit your religion.{/trap} Mujahid said they wanted him to {trap}be quiet about their gods and abandon the truth.{/trap} The verse names the offer so he would see it clearly.
now: Just skip prayer this once, the meeting is important. Just laugh along, it is only a joke. {trap}Small trades, each one reasonable.{/trap} {idea}Kindness to people is not the same as trading away what is true.{/idea}
old: A little compromise keeps the peace with everyone.
new: I can be gentle with people without bargaining away what is true.
try: Name one small thing you have been softening on to fit in. Decide to hold it this week.

title: The one who swears all the time is weak inside.
subtitle: Why constant oaths are a warning sign
then: The verse begins describing a type of man the people of Makkah knew. Ibn Kathir says the liar, {trap}due to his weakness and disgrace{/trap}, hides behind false oaths using Allah's names, and swears all the time without need. Ibn Abbas said mahin means {trap}the liar.{/trap}
now: I swear, wallahi, on my mother. You hear it in sales pitches and in your own mouth when you are late again. {trap}The more you need oaths, the less your word stands alone.{/trap} {idea}Plain truth needs no swearing.{/idea}
old: Swearing by Allah makes people believe me.
new: A truthful person's plain word is enough. Constant oaths cheapen Allah's name.
try: Go one full day without swearing by Allah in casual talk. Let your yes be yes.

title: He mocks people and carries tales between them.
subtitle: Gossip that breaks good relationships

row.title: corrupting good relations
sub: the Prophet ﷺ warned of it

then: Ibn Kathir explains this man goes around {trap}carrying tales to spoil relations between people{/trap} when they were good. The Prophet ﷺ passed two graves and said one of them was punished for {trap}spreading gossip.{/trap}
now: Did you hear what she said about you? A screenshot forwarded to the wrong chat. A whisper in the office kitchen. {trap}Two people who were fine are now cold.{/trap} {idea}The carrier is part of the damage.{/idea}
old: I only repeated what I heard.
new: Carrying words that break people apart is its own serious wrong.
try: The next time you hear something about someone, let it stop with you.

title: He blocks good, crosses limits, and dives into sin.
subtitle: Three faces of the same hard heart

row.title: I just keep what is mine

then: The description continues. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}he refuses to give and withholds the good he has{/trap}, he goes beyond the limits even in what is allowed, and {trap}he delves into forbidden things.{/trap}
now: The donation link you scroll past. The help you could give a junior colleague but do not. Telling a friend not to bother volunteering. {trap}Blocking good is quiet. Nobody calls it a sin.{/trap} {idea}The verse does.{/idea}
old: Not giving is not the same as doing harm.
new: Holding back good I could easily give is a real fault, not a neutral choice.
try: Give one small good you have been holding back today: a coin, a kind word, an hour.

title: Harsh, greedy, and known everywhere for his evil.
subtitle: When cruelty becomes what you are known for

row.title: a sheep with a cut ear
sub: easy to spot in the flock

then: Ibn Kathir says 'utul means {trap}cruel, harsh, greedy and stingy.{/trap} Ibn Abbas described a man of Quraysh who stood out for his evil like {trap}a sheep with a piece of its ear cut off.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said the people of Paradise are {reward}the weak and humble.{/reward}
now: Think of the person at work everyone warns new hires about. Known for one thing. {trap}Reputations are built one harsh reply at a time.{/trap} {idea}What would people say you are known for?{/idea}
old: Being tough and hard makes people respect me.
new: Harshness marks a person. Humility is what Allah honors.
try: Ask someone close to you, gently: is there a way I come across as harsh?
